messages:
sara_obs: Heads-up — our traces-derived SLO dashboard is ballooning costs. Storage + query egress is the culprit. Anyone on quick ideas for retention/sampling tradeoffs? :thinking_face:

aj_platform: ugh. are we storing full spans for every request? worth checking attribute sets we keep.

sara_obs: yes, currently we persist full OTLP payloads for 100% of spans for 30 days. we indexed http.route, model_id, and user_id which is hot.

devon_api: indexing user_id was probably overkill. recommended: drop PII from spans and only index model_id + route. user-level queries can be routed to logs.

kevin_prod: agree. also consider head-based sampling for steady-state and preserve 100% for error/non-2xx traces. tail-based SLOs need different approach though.

aj_platform: for SLOs derived from traces (latency percentiles) we should pre-aggregate at ingest: store p50/p95/p99 per route/bin per minute instead of full-span queries for dashboard. big query-cost win.

observability-bot: Deploy check — otel-collector config changed in staging: reduced attributes, added tail-based sampler for errors. CI passed.

sara_obs: Dev, can you sketch the pre-agg pipeline? how would we compute percentiles cheaply from spans?

devon_api: simplest: compute HDR histograms per route+model bucket in collector or a lightweight processor, export histogram metrics to prometheus/tsdb. Dashboard uses those metrics for SLOs, traces kept at lower retention.

aj_platform: exactly. pipeline: OTLP -> collector histogram processor -> metrics store (1d retention hot) + raw traces to long-term cheaper blob store (7d index, 90d cold).

kevin_prod: question: how do we reconcile error budget windows if metrics are aggregated differently than traces? we need stable mapping between a trace-derived latency and the metric histogram.

devon_api: include canonical span name and route tag in both histogram metrics and trace exports. use the same bucketing logic and timezone/windowing. tests validate equivalence on sampled subset.

aj_platform: also we need UX work in Console: when a user picks "Trace SLO", show a banner: "This SLO is backed by pre-aggregated trace histograms. Raw trace queries beyond X days may be sampled." Clear expectations reduce support tickets.

sara_obs: +1. rollout UX: default SLO should be metric-backed (less cost) with an option to use trace-backed SLOs for advanced cases. make trace-backed an opt-in with cost estimate.

kevin_prod: sampling strategy nit: prefer deterministic sampling keyed by route+trace_id hash so we can consistently sample across retries and services for span correlation.

devon_api: good call. hashing keeps whole trace intact. For head-based sampling, we can sample N requests per minute per route. For tail-based (errors/latency anomalies), we keep everything that exceeds thresholds.

aj_platform: exporters: should we keep Jaeger/Tempo/CQL for traces? Or just push raw OTLP to GCS/Parquet for cold storage and use Tempo for fast queries?

kevin_prod: Parquet + object store for long tail is cost efficient. Tempo for recent fast queries + index limited to model_id and route. Anything else should fallback to object search (expensive but rare).

observability-bot: Suggestion: add a "trace retention tier" per workspace in Console: Hot (14d indexed), Warm (30d reduced index), Cold (90d raw in object store).

sara_obs: That model sounds promising. we can surface estimated monthly cost per workspace based on request volume and chosen tiers. ops/sales will love that.

devon_api: small config example for otel-collector (pseudo):

```yaml
receivers:
  otlp:
    protocols:
      grpc: {}
processors:
  tail_sampling:
    policies:
      - name: error_and_latency
        type: latency
  histogram_agg:
    routes: ["/v1/generate","/v1/embed"]
exporters:
  otlp/metrics: {}
  otlp/traces: {}
service:
  pipelines:
    traces:
      receivers: [otlp]
      processors: [tail_sampling]
      exporters: [otlp/traces]
    metrics:
      receivers: [otlp]
      processors: [histogram_agg]
      exporters: [otlp/metrics]
```

aj_platform: nice. we should also include a scrubber to drop PII attributes and a config knob for "indexable_attributes" per org.

kevin_prod: ops question: how do we alert on error budget burn if traces are sampled? should still have a metrics fallback or synthetic pings.

sara_obs: we will maintain a metrics SLI (percentile from histograms) and a trace SLI for deep-dive. Alerting should use metrics SLI by default; trace SLI can have higher noise but be available.

devon_api: implementation task list: 1) change collector pipeline to add histogram aggregation & deterministic sampling 2) add scrubber & indexable_attributes config 3) console: retention tier UI + cost estimator 4) update docs & rollout notes 5) run A/B on a few large customers.

aj_platform: i'll take #3 and coordinate with growth for the estimator. sara, can you own the rollout notes?

sara_obs: yep. i'll draft the console copy and the "opt-in" flow.

kevin_prod: i'll handle collector changes & testing. we'll add a canary workspace flag first.

observability-bot: Action items recorded: collector-update, console-ui, docs, canary.

sara_obs: thanks all. this feels like a good bounded plan. we'll sync next week with rough ETA: collector change + canary in 2 weeks. :thumbsup:

aj_platform: quick follow-up — can we add a small example to docs showing how to compute SLOs from histogram metrics (promql)? saves a lot of questions later.

devon_api: will add. sample promql for p95 error budget: `histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(request_latency_seconds_bucket[5m])) by (le, route))`

sara_obs: perfect. closing thread for now unless blockers pop up. :party_parrot:
